title: Content-Based Router

validation.research: Five primary sources: Hohpe and Woolf’s Content-Based Router, Recipient List, and Message Filter catalogs; Apache Camel 4.22.x Choice documentation; RabbitMQ consumer acknowledgment and publisher-confirm documentation. The article distinguishes content-based selection from routing generally, single selected output from multiple intended recipients, and one-output filtering from choosing a destination. First-match is explicit policy supported by the Camel example, not a universal guarantee. Camel Choice is described as an implementation construct rather than a general alias.

example_limits: Original pure sequential order classifier. Input is an already-decoded exact five-field dictionary with integer schema 1, nonblank order ID and kind, Boolean express, and nonnegative integer US dollar cents. Kind matching is exact and case-sensitive. High-value review at 100000 cents precedes digital, express physical, standard physical, and otherwise classification review. Malformed shape or values select invalid-messages before business rules. A frozen Decision records one allowed logical channel, rule, and orders-v1. No enqueue, broker, parser, input-size enforcement, fulfillment, charging, business review, acknowledgment, retry, synchronization, or live policy updates. A policy version records selection; it does not pin replay execution or prevent duplicates. Production input parsing/size limits, stable message identity, authorization, handoff safety, bounded buffering, and repeated-effect handling remain implementation responsibilities. Camel header routing is an explanatory second context only.
publication: Local implementation only. No publishing, deployment, commit, push, or pull request.
